stories.text: Ralph Haunselyn founded an Augustinian priory at Shelford around 1160–80,[^founded] and by 1310–11 the church belonged to it. After Henry VIII dissolved the monasteries, the Stanhopes acquired the priory, in 1537, and with it the church. Lady Anne Stanhope's tomb, by Gabriel Royle, was put up after her death in 1588, and the family vault is dated 1677. In 1877–78 Lord Carnarvon paid for Ewan Christian to restore the church.

source.title: Shelford St Peter and St Paul: history (Southwell and Nottingham Church History Project)

stories.text: When Parliament's forces took Shelford House on 3 November 1645, Royalists led by a woman fired on them from the church tower; John Hutchinson had straw set alight to smoke them out, and smoke stains in the tower stairwell may date from then. Lady Anne Stanhope's monument and the font were damaged; the font was replaced in 1662.

283320.sum: St Peter and St Paul's Church, Shelford is a parish church in the Church of England in Shelford, Nottinghamshire. The church is Grade II* listed by the Department for Digital, Culture, Media and Sport.
